repairs.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Actual production source attachment repair for a layered 2D den animation, not a preview.
Reference image 1 is the approved intact low sandstone den, authoritative silhouette, style, pixel registration, palette and lighting. Reference image 2 is a defective separated base: its two support crowns have diagonal cut seams where the old roof boundary was retained. REPAIR THESE INCOMPLETE HIDDEN SURFACES.
Output one COMPLETE stationary base with the roof REMOVED, at the exact original square canvas and object registration of reference 1. Both left and right support rocks must have fully drawn coherent rounded angular top faces and hidden upper/back contours that were covered by the roof. Paint those sandstone planes continuously from crown to front faces with consistent upper-left light and warm brown contact shading. Eliminate every diagonal pasted-on band, duplicated dark roof edge, razor-thin ridge, black seam, alpha crack, chopped crown or flat mask cutoff. The inner dark rear wall must be a continuous complete surface between the supports, finished high enough behind the original roof line so a small roof tilt exposes real painted interior, not transparency or a pasted strip.
Preserve the intact source's exact base footprint, visible front faces, small foot pebbles, hollow interior floor, proportions and camera. The base stays low; do not add a pillar, tall wall, roof or bridge. Deep teal clean outlines, softly faceted honey-ochre sandstone and subtle painterly grain exactly match reference 1.
Keep the full original 1254-square composition and margins, no recentering or resizing. Genuine alpha transparency above and outside the completed base. No labels, text, grids, new objects, eggs, creatures, magic, external floor or shadow. This must be a complete reusable base attachment, not the cropped visible fragment.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Actual complete production roof attachment for a 2D layered stone-den animation, not a preview.
Reference image 1: approved intact low sandstone den; exact source shape, palette, camera, outline, lighting and pixel registration. Reference image 2: defective extracted roof attachment; its bottom contour is an incomplete crop with tiny notches and dangling outline fragments at contact points.
Output ONLY the large broad top sandstone slab, isolated in the EXACT original square canvas, scale, angle and position of reference 1. Remove supports and all lower-den content. Preserve every visible top plane and outer upper silhouette of the approved slab. Complete the slab's lower front lip and the hidden lower corners/underside behind both supporting stones as a coherent solid closed rock. The slab has real subtle thickness: a continuous warm dark ochre underside/contact face with a clean dark-teal lower contour, no cutouts, no missing triangular corners, no pasted strip, no floating line, no spikes, and no alpha crack through the slab. Reconstruct only the small concealed lower surfaces; do not inflate the roof, thicken it excessively, change perspective or make a new design.
All parts of the complete roof are one rigid source attachment. Its hidden lower areas will be drawn behind foreground supporting stones during animation. The upper face has the same cream upper-left light and painterly facets as the approved source, the underside follows that light coherently with darker warm contact shading.
Original 1254-square registration and transparent margins. Genuine alpha transparency, one roof slab only. No base, supports, pebbles, terrain, labels, text, diagrams, arrows or comparison panels.

rearWallPrompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Paint one real hidden-surface source attachment for the inside rear wall of this sandstone den.
The approved original den in image 1 establishes exact square 1254x1254 source registration, camera, scale, sandstone texture and light. Image 2 is the separated base and establishes the lower interior palette. The rear wall was drawn only up to the old visible roof edge, leaving an UNPAINTED GAP when the roof tips upward. Repair by drawing a COMPLETE TALLER RECESSED INNER REAR WALL that extends well behind the roof.
Output ONLY that rear inner wall attachment, no roof, no supports, no floor, no exterior props. In the original square registration, it occupies approximately x=350 to 930 and y=590 to 960: a broad continuous opaque shallow recessed sandstone wall, gently narrowing at the bottom. Its top runs from about (360,600) to (920,630), much HIGHER than the old diagonal visible edge. Left and right edges and bottom may be simple fully closed stone contours because supporting stones, roof and floor occlude them. Give ample painted overlap. No hole, no transparent slit, and no unpainted band anywhere inside this wall. The wall must be an opaque continuous warm dark ochre/brown surface with subtly faceted broad planes and original soft painterly texture. The upper area is darker from roof shadow, the lower area gently warmer toward the original den floor. No black void and no sharp artificial rectangular gradient.
Everything outside this single wall piece is true alpha transparency. Keep the complete source canvas and exact registration; do not recenter it or make a standalone enlarged stone. Match image 1 color, subtle grain and lighting. This is a reusable production rear-wall attachment which will be placed BEHIND the base and moving roof. No labels, text, border, arrows, scene, eggs, characters, crystals or effects.
